Bucharest (the capital and largest city of Romania)
to bring up, to rear, to educate
to educate, to train (someone to be someone)
approach, playing to the gallery (movements to gain favor; advances)
heaven, utopia (place where everything is perfect)
golden mean (position of balance between excess and deficiency)
to fall (upon, on), to pounce (on), to attack, to assault, to go (for)
to come down (on), to jump (on), to jump all over
to begin, to start, to set in, to break out
period of not leaving a given city or country
prohibition on leaving a given city or country
a male given name, Nikodim, equivalent to English Nicodemus
whoops!; oops! (as when stumbling and almost tripping or almost stepping on something to be avoided)
alley-oop (also used as an exclamation when dogs do tricks)

a man who is overly concerned with his sex life; a man who is unsuccessfully trying to find sex partners

capable (at), able, apt (at), gifted (at/in), talented (at) (having ability (in))

rich, bountiful (in terms of harvest; of land or time)

the pronunciation of unstressed /e/ or /a/ after a palatalised consonant before the stressed syllable as /a/ rather than /i/, e.g. несли́ (neslí) is pronounced [nʲas⁽ʲ⁾ˈlʲi], not [nʲɪs⁽ʲ⁾ˈlʲi]. This occurs in some Russian dialects (only where а́канье (ákanʹje) is also present) and in standard Belarusian.
